change: Replaced the first-party libc umask unsafe block with rustix::process::umask, retaining raw mode bits and the previous-mask return value.
dependency: Enabled process on already-pinned rustix 1.1.5; existing std/fs/use-libc features and Cargo.lock package versions are unchanged. cargo deny --all-features check and cargo audit passed.
source_evidence: rustix 1.1.5 src/process/umask.rs delegates to backend/process/syscalls.rs. Its libc backend casts mask.bits() to libc mode_t, calls libc::umask once, and returns Mode::from_bits_retain of the result. The toolkit retains the existing input/output casts.
fixture: Dedicated osd_umask_api_behavior test executable isolates process-global mask changes. Baseline and replacement passed on Linux x86_64: three mask/creation-mode cases, previous-mask sequencing, and u32::MAX masked to 0777. The original process mask is restored on success; a panic exits this isolated test process.
trust: Established rustix/libc unsafe remains separately trusted and inventoried; no custom first-party unsafe was relocated. Enabling process exposes more dependency code and requires full workspace and native validation.
inventory: Expected native_unix source blocks 15 to 14; compiler spans Linux 28 to 26 and macOS 24 to 22 against this baseline. Windows unchanged. Full verification pending.
deletion: Old direct umask call deleted in this increment; no parallel implementation retained. Current migration milestone is the limit.
validation: Focused Linux fixture, dependency checks and cargo xtask pr passed; local gate log /tmp/martensite-umask-pr.log. Independent standards and spec reviews found no production-code defects; the evidence status was updated after review. Native matrix remains pending.
exclusions: No public API or package version change
Existing process-wide umask semantics are preserved, not redesigned as operation-local state
No Miri claim for the native process call
